dogecoin.text:
A memecoin is more asymmetric the more people who don’t own it reference it. Eg. Traditional finance, mainstream media, newspapers, etc.

The last time this happened, the meme in question almost hit $100B — Dogecoin. 

This is happening with Fartcoin now.
Sitting at just $1B.

@notputsandcalls It’s a memecoin — That’s what traditional media always calls them. 

Doesn’t stop them from appreciating though. Eg. Dogecoin in 2020.

As a narrative, if you spread too thin by doing too much, your token loses its memetics.

Fartcoin is where it is because it’s just Fartcoin. Dogecoin is where it is because it’s just a picture of a dog. Bitcoin is where it is because it serves a single purpose.

The last time a meme had all these catalysts, it was literally dogecoin. 

That’s at $50B now.

The dev of dogecoin didn’t create the doge (shiba inu) meme.

The dev of pepe didn’t create the pepe the frog meme. 

You do realise that the dev of troll didn’t create the troll-face meme.

I.e. It doesn’t matter who the original artist is. What matters is which community
